items.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: And of course Joe Zawinul has done wonderful things over the years.

ctx.x: I like that term you just said, “borderline jazz.” Maybe that should be the name in the record bins, instead of “new age” instead of “fusion,” we’ll call it “borderline jazz.”

Well you know I don’t just categorically — a lot of people my age in my generation do just categorically rule out a lot of types of musical trends. I’ve tried to stay away from that over the years. I guess I have pretty eclectic tastes. I love a lot of different kinds of music and a lot of different genres, if it’s honest, if it’s real. And I think most of us know when it’s real pretty quickly, and we know when it’s not. And in the — whatever you want to call it — of course in the 70s, when it first started…
Trying to jump on some bandwagon perhaps? Although I don’t know how big the wagon is.
